The evidence indicates that Spironolactone, as an aldosterone antagonist, is included in the class of drugs that interact with Nr3c2. Eplerenone, a known aldosterone antagonist, binds to Nr3c2, implying that the interaction between aldosterone antagonists and Nr3c2 is a common pathway. The lowest common ancestor of Spironolactone and Eplerenone is the lactone class, suggesting a shared structural feature that may contribute to their ability to interact with Nr3c2. This integrated evidence suggests that Spironolactone may act through a mechanism similar to Eplerenone, potentially by modulating Nr3c2 activity. The relationship is supported by the structural and functional overlap between these drugs, and the shared pathway of interaction with Nr3c2.
